questions.question: MCP compresses tool integration from M×N glue into M+N. What does "N" refer to?
options: The number of tools (each implements one server)
questions.explanation: See the "Three roles: host, client, server" section: the tool side implements a server once (corresponding to N tools), the app side implements a client once (corresponding to M apps); M apps × N tools become M+N rather than M×N.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of MCP's three capability classes?
questions.explanation: See the "Capability negotiation and the three capability classes" section: MCP's three capability classes are tools (executable actions), resources (readable data), and prompts (pre-made prompt templates); "functions" is not a protocol-level MCP capability class.

questions.question: Regarding the similarities and differences between MCP and an ordinary tool call, which statement is correct?
options: The model must be aware of protocol details to know which server a tool lives on
Everything on the model side (tool list, request, feedback, id pairing) is preserved; MCP is fully transparent to the model
MCP only supports tools inside the same process
A server must return the same error codes as the client
questions.explanation: See the "Versus an ordinary tool call" section: everything on the model side — tool list, tool_use request, tool_result feedback, id pairing — stays the same; MCP is fully transparent to the model. The differences live on the integration side (protocol, lifecycle, network round trip, error translation, etc.).
